metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: Child 734d allowlist: 'The single-ticket MCP tool set mirrors the CLI allowlist: `show_ticket`, ... `archive_ticket`, `check_ac`.'
Child 734d Scope: 'src/rebar/_mcp_models.py — add `cross_session_warning: str | None = None` to `WriteAckOut` and `TicketStateOut`.' (no `GateResultOut`)
Codebase: `check_ac` MCP handler returns `GateResultOut` (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:406), which is neither WriteAckOut nor TicketStateOut
findings.finding: Child 734d lists `check_ac` in its single-ticket MCP allowlist that should carry `cross_session_warning`, but its Approach/Scope only add the field to `WriteAckOut` and `TicketStateOut`; the `check_ac` handler returns `GateResultOut` (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:406), which is never given the field — so `check_ac` cannot actually carry the warning as the allowlist implies.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `cross_session_warning: str | None = None` to `GateResultOut` and populate it in the `check_ac` handler, or drop `check_ac` from 734d's allowlist to match the CLI/MCP/library reconciliation.

evidence: 5d55 Approach: 'add the stderr emit at each allowlisted command's resolved-id point (which may be require_id ... or a command's own id-resolution arm)' and 'the frozenset membership check - not a require_id call - is what excludes bulk commands ... not a single shared id-resolution helper.'
3d8a Surface layering: 'execute() runs _maybe_warn_cross_session (the allowlist single source) and handler dispatch inside suppress_cross_session_warning()'
The two children disagree on whether the CLI advisory is emitted at each command's own id-resolution arm (5d55) or by one centralized name-keyed helper in execute() (3d8a).
findings.finding: Children 5d55 and 3d8a describe two incompatible CLI emit architectures for the same seam. 5d55's Approach mandates a PER-COMMAND resolved-id insertion and explicitly states it is 'not a single shared id-resolution helper', while 3d8a describes a single centralized helper (_maybe_warn_cross_session, 'the allowlist single source') run inside execute().
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt one architecture in both children: since 3d8a's dedup requires a single wrap point, revise 5d55's Approach to specify a single centralized name-keyed helper at the dispatch layer (e.g. _maybe_warn_cross_session in _cli/_execute.py) rather than per-command resolved-id insertions.

evidence: CLI child 5d55: allowlist 'covers ... `show`, `comment`, `edit`, `transition`, `reopen`, `tag`, `untag`, `set-file-impact`, `declare-no-file-impact`, `deps`, `archive`, `check-ac`, `clarity-check`, `link`, `unlink`'

Library child 3d8a: 'the read `show_ticket` ... and `deps`; the writes transition / reopen ... comment, edit, tag, untag, set_file_impact, declare_no_file_impact, link ... unlink ... archive' — no `check_ac`, no `clarity_check`
MCP child 734d: 'mirrors the CLI allowlist: `show_ticket`, `comment_ticket`, ... `archive_ticket`, `check_ac`' — no `ticket_deps`, no `clarity_check`

Codebase confirms all three exist per surface: `rebar.deps`/`rebar.check_ac`/`rebar.clarity_check` (src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:172, src/rebar/_lib_gates.py:35/61); MCP `ticket_deps`/`clarity_check`/`check_ac` (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:313/400/406); CLI `clarity-check` (src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:246)
findings.finding: The three surface children each state their single-ticket allowlist 'mirrors' the others, but the enumerated allowlists diverge: `deps`/`ticket_deps` is included on CLI (5d55) and library (3d8a) but absent from MCP (734d); `check_ac`/`check-ac` is included on CLI (5d55) and MCP (734d) but absent from library (3d8a); `clarity-check`/`clarity_check` is included on CLI (5d55) but absent from both MCP and library.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the canonical single-ticket allowlist once (e.g. in the detector story 0804 or the parent), enumerate exactly which single-ticket ops warn, and have each surface child reference that one list rather than restating a divergent set.

evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py: 3d8a-5a5d-8773-473d & 5d55-15ab-8ec1-4622 (no ordering edge)
findings.finding: Sibling tickets touch the same file(s) with no ordering edge.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a depends_on/blocks edge to serialize, or partition the file ownership.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

evidence: Parent decomposition: 'Each child owns a distinct, non-overlapping seam (reducer state, pure detector+config, CLI rendering, MCP model/schema, library warnings channel).'
Parent decomposition declares CLI/MCP/library children each only 'Depends on the detector' — no inter-sibling dependency stated.

Library child Scope: 'src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py — hold suppress_cross_session_warning() across detection + dispatch so the library never doubles the CLI WARN: line.' and 'src/rebar/mcp_server.py — build_server() wraps read/write tool registration with the suppress_library_double_advisory proxy.'
Library child dedup AC asserts against a CLI test file: 'a warning CLI command (e.g. link) writes exactly one WARN: line ... (test_cross_session_cli.py count(...) == 1).'
findings.finding: The library child owns cross-cutting suppression edits to the CLI and MCP surface files, creating a hidden inter-sibling dependency and scope overlap that contradicts the parent's 'distinct, non-overlapping seam' decomposition and its 'each depends only on the detector' ordering.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the parent decomposition (and in 3d8a) that dedup/suppression is a cross-surface concern owned by the library child which depends on and must sequence after the CLI and MCP children; or relocate the CLI/MCP suppression wrapping into their respective surface children so each surface owns its own dedup.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add explicit depends_on edges from 3d8a to 5d55 (CLI) and 734d (MCP), or relocate the CLI/MCP dedup wrappers into 5d55/734d respectively, so the single-emit dedup cannot land before the surface emit it deduplicates.
evidence: 3d8a Scope: 'src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py - hold suppress_cross_session_warning() across detection + dispatch so the library never doubles the CLI WARN: line.'
3d8a Scope: 'src/rebar/mcp_server.py - build_server() wraps read/write tool registration with the suppress_library_double_advisory proxy'
5d55 Scope owns 'src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py - single dispatch choke point: allowlist frozenset + best-effort stderr WARN emit'
3d8a AC: 'Single-emit dedup: a warning CLI command (e.g. link) writes exactly one WARN: line, not doubled by the library channel' -- presupposes 5d55's WARN: emit exists
3d8a deps (per ticket state) list only depends_on 0804-9a6b-9182-42c9; no depends_on 5d55 or 734d.
findings.finding: Child 3d8a's Scope modifies src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py and src/rebar/mcp_server.py -- the same CLI dispatch and MCP registration seams that the CLI surface (5d55) and MCP surface (734d) own the emit for -- to add the single-emit dedup suppression, yet 3d8a declares depends_on only the detector (0804), not 5d55 or 734d. The dedup wrapper is meaningless (and its dedup AC untestable) unless the CLI `WARN:` emit (5d55) and MCP `cross_session_warning` field (734d) already exist to be deduplicated against.
scenarios: If 3d8a lands before 5d55, the CLI dedup wrapper suppresses a library warning that would otherwise be the sole CLI advisory, and no WARN: line is emitted at all -- the dedup AC ('count == 1') passes vacuously with count 0 during that window.
If 734d has not yet added the MCP response field, 3d8a's mcp_server proxy suppresses the library channel leaving the MCP surface with no advisory.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare 3d8a depends_on 5d55 and 734d (the dedup is inherently downstream of both emits), or move the `suppress_cross_session_warning()` wrapping of `_execute.py` into 5d55 and the `suppress_library_double_advisory` wrapping of `mcp_server.py` into 734d, keeping each surface's dedup with the surface that introduces the emit.

evidence: CLI child Scope covers only 'The CLI dispatch layer under src/rebar/_cli/ — define the allowlist frozenset ... and add the stderr emit' and 'docs/user-guide.md' — no mention of the library CrossSessionWarning doubling or its suppression.
CLI child depends line: 'Depends on the detector ... and on the reducer clearing.' — the library child is not named as a dependency.
Library child asserts the CLI single-emit invariant: 'a warning CLI command (e.g. link) writes exactly one WARN: line, not doubled by the library channel.'

Repo confirmation: src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py wraps _maybe_warn_cross_session + _invoke in suppress_cross_session_warning(), and CLI handlers dispatch to instrumented library mutators that would otherwise emit CrossSessionWarning.
findings.finding: The CLI child's spec relies on suppression it neither owns nor mentions: its behavior (a single WARN line) is only correct once the library channel is suppressed, but that suppression is specified in the library child, leaving a dependency gap in the CLI child.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the suppression-wrapper edit to the CLI child's Scope and name library-channel suppression as its responsibility, or explicitly declare the CLI child depends on the library child for dedup.

evidence: MCP child Approach: single-ticket handlers call 'cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, ...)' then perform 'rebar.<op>(...)' — the library op it invokes is the one the library child (3d8a) instruments to emit CrossSessionWarning.
MCP child Scope and depends line name only the detector and reducer clearing; no mention of the library-channel double emission or its suppression.
Library child Scope: 'src/rebar/mcp_server.py — build_server() wraps read/write tool registration with the suppress_library_double_advisory proxy (scoped per-handler suppression; no global filter).'
Repo confirmation: _mcp_writes.py:290-306 transition_ticket calls _cross_session(ticket_id) AND rebar.transition(...) (instrumented).
findings.finding: The MCP child computes its own warning AND dispatches to instrumented library mutators, so without the library child's suppress_library_double_advisory proxy the MCP process double-emits (response field plus stdlib CrossSessionWarning); this coupling/dependency is unstated in the MCP child.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the library-double-advisory suppression as an explicit dependency of the MCP child, or move the per-handler suppression into the MCP child so the MCP surface owns its own dedup end to end.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the reducer-clearing change is reversible (derived state recomputed from the append-only log by reverting the fold) and note any consumers that read claimed_session on non-in_progress tickets, or confirm none exist.
evidence: 'the claim-session provenance is cleared on every exit from in_progress'
'a non-in_progress ticket never reports a stale holder'
Unlike the warning feature (config toggle escape hatch), the reducer clearing has no toggle and no stated rollback path
findings.finding: The reducer-clearing story changes existing derived-state semantics (claimed_session/claim_harness/claim_remote_session now cleared on every exit from in_progress) without an explicit rollback/back-out or expand-contract note, even though it alters what consumers reading claimed_session on non-in_progress tickets will observe.
scenarios: A downstream consumer or report reads claimed_session on a closed/blocked ticket expecting the historical claimer and now gets empty
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line rollback note to the Reducer clearing child: reverting the fold change restores prior projection since events are append-only and unchanged; confirm no consumer depends on claimed_session persisting after in_progress exit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the 3d8a mcp_server.py dedup contradiction: make the file_impact reason match the description (scoped per-handler suppression via suppress_library_double_advisory, no process-global filter).
evidence: 3d8a description: 'suppress_library_double_advisory(mcp) ... so the response field is the only MCP advisory WITHOUT a process-global filter (which would over-silence the library CrossSessionWarning for unrelated import rebar callers sharing the server process).'
3d8a file_impact reason (mcp_server.py): 'build_server() ignores CrossSessionWarning process-wide so the library channel does not double the MCP response field'
findings.finding: Child 3d8a carries an internal contradiction about the MCP dedup mechanism that also governs its handshake with the MCP surface (734d): the description and AC specify a per-tool-handler proxy 'WITHOUT a process-global filter (which would over-silence the library CrossSessionWarning for unrelated import rebar callers sharing the server process)', but 3d8a's file_impact reason for mcp_server.py states 'build_server() ignores CrossSessionWarning process-wide so the library channel does not double the MCP response field' -- i.e. the exact process-global filter the prose forbids.
scenarios: If implemented per the file_impact reason (process-wide ignore), an unrelated `import rebar` caller in the same server process is silently denied its CrossSessionWarning -- the over-silencing the description explicitly set out to avoid, and a consumer-impact regression on the library channel that 734d relies on being intact.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the 3d8a mcp_server.py file_impact reason to describe the per-handler `suppress_library_double_advisory` proxy and drop the 'ignores CrossSessionWarning process-wide' wording so the seam is unambiguously scoped.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the single-ticket operation set across CLI/MCP/library at the parent (or explicitly amend parent AC3 to name the MCP-deferred verbs check_ac/quality_check/declare_no_file_impact and the absent deps/clarity MCP handlers as an accepted per-surface limitation with the follow-up ticket cited).
evidence: Parent AC3: 'The warning is surfaced for single-ticket-targeted operations on CLI (stderr line), MCP (structured response field), and library (warnings.warn)'
734d Approach: 'check_ac and quality_check ... declare_no_file_impact ... These three are deferred to the follow-up'
5d55 allowlist includes 'deps', 'check-ac', 'clarity-check'
3d8a Scope emits from '_lib_gates.py - ... set_file_impact, declare_no_file_impact, clarity_check, check_ac' and '_lib_reads.py - ... deps'
734d single-ticket tool list has no deps and no clarity gate handler entry
findings.finding: The MCP surface child (734d) narrows the single-ticket operation set relative to the CLI (5d55) and library (3d8a) siblings, so several single-ticket operations warn on CLI/library but never surface a warning on MCP. 734d explicitly defers check_ac, quality_check, and declare_no_file_impact; it also lists no deps/get-deps or clarity-check tool, whereas 5d55's allowlist includes deps/check-ac/clarity-check and 3d8a emits from deps/check_ac/clarity_check/declare_no_file_impact. The parent AC3 requires the warning 'surfaced for single-ticket-targeted operations on ... MCP' without carving these out, and the epic's own deferral rationale is documented only inside child 734d, not reconciled against the sibling scope.
scenarios: A session-B `check_ac`/`clarity_check`/`declare_no_file_impact` against an A-held ticket warns on CLI stderr and via library warnings.warn but returns no cross_session_warning to an MCP client, who cannot see CLI stderr.
A session-B `deps <id>` warns on CLI and library but the MCP client gets no advisory.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend 734d to carry cross_session_warning on the gate/deps single-ticket MCP tools (accepting the GateResultOut/str schema changes), or update the parent AC3 to codify the surface-parity carve-out and reference the discovered_from follow-up so the completion verifier does not read AC3 as requiring uniform MCP coverage.
